explanations.text:
The skill claude reads when you give an abstraction and want the code under it.

  you: "/human an http server using python that returns hello world"
       claude keeps your words as they are, in abstraction.txt at the root —
       no spelling fixed, no word trimmed                             ([the skill](human))
       claude writes the code files, no comments; the gate is static like a
       compiler's — the file must parse — and there is no run and no test
       the tool registers the project: the file list, the reader, the empty
       project map
       claude maps the detailed telling of each file, in a shape from the
       catalog beside this skill — the rail by default          ([the shape](The rail shape))
       claude maps your words on top, with pins in them; the gate strips the
       pins and compares the rest to abstraction.txt character for character —
       a changed word is a refusal, and the entry is marked as yours, so a
       later repair of the code leaves its words alone
       when the project has more than one file, claude maps one telling of
       the project — what you can ask for and which file answers each part
       claude reports each file and the project, and gives you the reader
                                                                      ([the run](The run))

  the pins tie a few words to a block, an earlier entry, another file, or an
  entry of another file's map; unique words, real targets, no circle, the
  detailed entry before the plainer one                              ([the pins](Pins))

  afterwards: sync runs exactly once per change; a reword of your abstraction
  goes to abstraction.txt first; a repair may re-pin your words but never
  change them                                                        ([the rules](Rules))
